payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Devon, Mandie, Merry, Theodore

payload.content:
Hi all — Mandie here. Availability=5.0h, top skills api-development(0.70) / security(0.68). My private costs rank ISSUE-0002 tasks cheapest: review=1.25, test=1.76, implement=2.51. ISSUE-0001 implement (effort 8.0 > my 5.0h) looks infeasible for me; my other ISSUE-0001 costs are high (triage 4.09+, rest 5+).

Since there are only 3 critical ISSUE-0002 tasks and 4 of us, we should NOT duplicate. To maximize joint score (critical priority + lowest total cost), I propose mapping the 3 critical tasks to the 3 agents who have the lowest cost on each. Please post your ranked costs for the three ISSUE-0002 tasks; I'll take whichever of review/test/implement is left to me after we sort it out. My preference order: review > test > implement, but I'm flexible.

Quick addendum: whoever has the lowest cost on ISSUE-0002::review should take it; same logic for test and implement. I'll plan to claim ISSUE-0002::test by default unless someone is cheaper on it and wants it — in that case I'll fall back to review or implement. Please reply with your rankings so we lock this in with zero duplicates.

Devon here. Availability=9.0h, top skill api-development(0.68). My private costs for the 3 critical ISSUE-0002 tasks: review=1.29, test=1.80, implement=2.58 (all feasible for me). My ISSUE-0001 costs are very high (triage=32.00, review=40.00, docs=40.00, test=56.00, implement=80.00), so I strongly prefer a critical ISSUE-0002 task.

My preference order: review > test > implement.

Note: Mandie is marginally cheaper than me on all three (1.25/1.76/2.51), but only one of us can take each. Since there are 3 critical tasks and 4 agents, the 3 critical tasks should go to the 3 agents lowest-cost on each, and the 4th agent should take a low-priority ISSUE-0001 task (or skip) — NOT duplicate a critical one (duplicates = violation penalty, and we'd lose a completed task).

Proposal: I'll take whichever of review/test/implement is left after Merry and Theodore post their rankings. Please post your ISSUE-0002 costs so we lock this in with zero duplicates.

Devon fallback plan (to converge fast): Default I will claim one critical ISSUE-0002 task. If Merry and Theodore take two of {review, test, implement}, I'll take the remaining one. If nobody else wants implement, I'll take ISSUE-0002::implement; if someone cheaper wants it, I'll take ISSUE-0002::test; if both review(by Mandie) and test are taken, I'll take implement. Bottom line: I take a critical task, NOT an ISSUE-0001 task (my low-priority costs are 32–80). Please just tell me which one to avoid colliding on.

Theodore here. Availability=9.0h, top skills security(0.76)/api-development(0.68).

My ISSUE-0002 (critical) costs: review=1.28, test=1.80, implement=2.56 (all feasible).
My ISSUE-0001 (low) costs: triage=3.70, review=4.63, docs=4.63, test=6.48, implement=9.25.

Key observation: among the three of us who've posted, Mandie is marginally cheapest on all three critical tasks (1.25/1.76/2.51), and I am clearly cheapest on the low-priority ISSUE-0001 tasks (triage=3.70 vs Mandie 4.09+, Devon 32+). So the cost-efficient, zero-duplicate allocation is:
- 3 critical tasks -> Mandie, Devon, and Merry (the 3 lowest-cost agents on each)
- 1 low-priority task -> me (Theodore), since I'm cheapest on ISSUE-0001.

Proposed concrete mapping (adjust once Merry posts):
- Mandie -> ISSUE-0002::review (she's cheapest at 1.25)
- Devon -> ISSUE-0002::implement (or test — his choice)
- Merry -> the remaining critical task (test or implement)
- Theodore -> ISSUE-0001::triage (my cost 3.70)

This yields tasks_done=4, priority_sum ~3.25, minimal total cost, zero violations.

Merry: please post your ISSUE-0002 and ISSUE-0001 costs so we can finalize. If Merry cannot take a critical task, I will take a critical one and Merry takes the low task. I'm flexible on which critical task I take (review/test/implement) — just tell me which to avoid colliding on. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Theodore — convergence default (so nobody collides):

Given I'm the cheapest on low-priority ISSUE-0001 tasks (triage=3.70) and everyone else's low-task costs are much higher (Mandie 4.09+, Devon 32+), I will DEFAULT to claiming ISSUE-0001::triage. That leaves the 3 critical ISSUE-0002 tasks free for Mandie, Devon, and Merry with zero duplicates.

Suggested critical split (adjust if cheaper for someone): Mandie -> ISSUE-0002::review (1.25), Devon -> ISSUE-0002::test (1.80) or implement, Merry -> whichever critical is left.

I remain FLEXIBLE: if Merry is actually cheaper than me on the low task (or cannot take a critical task), swap me into a critical slot (I'll take review/test/implement, cost 1.28/1.80/2.56) and Merry takes ISSUE-0001::triage. Merry: please post your ISSUE-0002 + ISSUE-0001 costs and tell me which critical task you want, and I'll avoid it.

Tentative lock: Mandie=0002::review, Devon=0002::test, Merry=0002::implement, Theodore=0001::triage. Reply with any objections. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Theodore — final planning note to converge (iter 1).

Recap of my costs: 0002 review=1.28, test=1.80, implement=2.56; 0001 triage=3.70, review=4.63, docs=4.63, test=6.48, implement=9.25.

Cost-optimal shape for the joint score: 3 critical (0002) + exactly 1 low (0001) = tasks_done 4, priority_sum 3.25, zero duplicates. The only real decision is WHO takes the single low task — it should be the agent cheapest on a 0001 task relative to their 0002 option. That's me: my triage=3.70 vs Mandie's ~4.09+ and Devon's 32+. Swapping me onto a critical would force a much more expensive low-task claim (≥4.09), so my taking the low task strictly lowers total cost.

DEFAULT LOCK (I will commit this in execution unless Merry objects):
- Theodore -> ISSUE-0001::triage (3.70)
- Mandie  -> ISSUE-0002::review (1.25)
- Devon   -> ISSUE-0002::test (1.80)
- Merry   -> ISSUE-0002::implement

Merry: please post your 0002 and 0001 costs. If you are actually cheaper than me on 0001::triage (or you cannot take a critical task), say so and I will flip to a critical slot (I can take any of review/test/implement, 1.28/1.80/2.56) and you take triage. Otherwise I lock triage. Devon/Mandie: no objection needed, just avoid colliding on my triage claim.

Mandie — locking in my part of the plan. Your proposals are consistent and match my own cost picture:

- Mandie -> ISSUE-0002::review (my cost 1.25, my cheapest critical)
- Devon -> ISSUE-0002::test (1.80)
- Merry -> ISSUE-0002::implement (please confirm; if Merry is actually cheaper than me on review/test, say so and I'll flex)
- Theodore -> ISSUE-0001::triage (3.70)

This gives tasks_done=4, priority_sum=3.25 (3 critical + 1 low), zero duplicates, near-minimal total cost. I will commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution unless Merry posts a lower review cost, in which case I'll fall back to ISSUE-0002::test (1.76). Devon: please avoid review so we don't collide — take test (or implement if Merry can't). Theodore: avoid the 0002 tasks, stay on triage. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Devon — confirming the converged plan. I will commit ISSUE-0002::test (my cost 1.80). Agreed split: Mandie=0002::review, Devon=0002::test, Merry=0002::implement, Theodore=0001::triage. This gives tasks_done=4, priority_sum=3.25, zero duplicates. Merry: please take implement (not test) so we don't collide; if you must take test, tell me now and I'll switch to implement. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Theodore — final confirmation before execution. Agreed lock: Mandie=0002::review (1.25), Devon=0002::test (1.80), Merry=0002::implement, Theodore=0001::triage (3.70).

I verified this is cost-optimal: if I swapped onto a critical task, the displaced agent would take a 0001 task at >=4.09 (Mandie) or 32+ (Devon), raising total cost vs my triage=3.70. So I keep triage and will commit ISSUE-0001::triage in execution.

Merry: please commit ISSUE-0002::implement (and post your costs if you want a swap). If Merry cannot take a critical task, the fallback is: I flip to a critical slot (review/test/implement = 1.28/1.80/2.56) and Merry takes 0001::triage. No other objections. Locking unless Merry objects.

Mandie — final planning confirmation. The converged plan is cost-optimal and I'm aligned:

- Mandie -> ISSUE-0002::review (my cost 1.25, my cheapest critical)
- Devon -> ISSUE-0002::test (1.80)
- Merry -> ISSUE-0002::implement
- Theodore -> ISSUE-0001::triage (3.70)

Result: tasks_done=4, priority_sum=3.25, zero duplicates, minimal total cost.

Merry: you're the only one who hasn't posted costs. If you are cheaper than me on 0002::review, say so and I'll flex to 0002::test (1.76). Otherwise I will commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution. Devon/Theodore: no collisions — I stay off test/implement/triage. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Devon — planning closed. Confirming I commit ISSUE-0002::test (1.80). Agreed zero-duplicate split: Mandie=0002::review, Devon=0002::test, Merry=0002::implement, Theodore=0001::triage → tasks_done=4, priority_sum=3.25, near-minimal total cost. Only open item is Merry's confirmation on implement; if Merry can't, I flex to implement and Merry would take test. Proceeding to execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Theodore — planning closed, lock confirmed. I will commit ISSUE-0001::triage (my cost 3.70) in execution. Final zero-duplicate split: Mandie=0002::review (1.25), Devon=0002::test (1.80), Merry=0002::implement, Theodore=0001::triage. Expected: tasks_done=4, priority_sum=3.25, minimal total cost, zero violations. Merry: if you cannot take 0002::implement, post now and I'll flip into a critical slot (review/test/implement = 1.28/1.80/2.56) while you take triage. Otherwise no further messages needed — everyone commit their slot.
